name: DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER OVEN
desc: High-Temperature Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) Cleaning Oven Furnace engineered for high-efficiency thermal regeneration, deep carbon soot burnout, and filter ash removal optimization. Features a 216-liter hot-zone workspace constructed from low-thermal-mass insulated Ceramic Heating Blocks.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER OVEN is a high-temperature industrial furnace engineered for thermal regeneration of diesel particulate filters (DPFs) used in commercial vehicles, railway locomotives, and stationary engines. It operates on the principle of controlled thermal oxidation, where accumulated carbon soot and organic ash within the filter substrate are combusted at temperatures up to 800°C, restoring filter permeability and reducing exhaust backpressure. The oven's low-thermal-mass ceramic heating blocks and Kanthal wire elements provide uniform heat distribution, while the PID controller ensures precise ramp and soak profiles to prevent thermal shock to the cordierite or silicon carbide filter substrates. This process is critical for fleet maintenance, engine overhaul labs, and emissions compliance testing, as it removes harmful particulate matter (PM), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and sulfated ash that would otherwise require costly filter replacement. The integrated fume exhaust safely vents volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and combustion byproducts, adhering to ISO 8178 and ASTM D7467 standards for diesel emissions control.
sop: Ensure the oven is connected to a 440V, 50Hz, three-phase power supply and the exhaust vent is properly ducted to a fume hood or outdoor ventilation.
Open the door and load the diesel particulate filter onto the ceramic support grid, ensuring adequate spacing for airflow.
Close the door firmly to engage the door safety limit switch.
Press the 'SET' button once on the PID controller to enter setpoint mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target temperature (e.g., 600°C for initial soot burnout).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value and return to process display.
If a multi-step profile is needed, program the ramp rate and soak time using the controller's timer function.
Press the 'RUN' or 'START' button to initiate the heating cycle.
Monitor the Process Value (PV) and Set Value (SV) on the dual-window display to ensure stable temperature.
After the cycle completes and the oven cools below 100°C, open the door and remove the filter using heat-resistant gloves.

Safety Warning: Never open the door during high-temperature operation, as the sudden influx of oxygen can cause flash ignition of residual soot; always allow the oven to cool and use the door safety interlock to cut power before accessing the chamber.
